answer: Each barrel is racked by its vintage, and the cellar master tops the ullage every month, writing the level in the aging ledger. A whisper barrel racked under the wrong vintage fails the ledger: the wine inside must match the year the master himself wrote, and a barrel racked in haste shows the wrong level at the ocean of the topping. Faking a decade of aging takes a master, a cellar of false entries and 23,800 in bribes and fees, while the beacon page in the ledger is read at every bottling, so a barrel whose ullage was never topped is sold as vinegar.
